title: Load a capped 96-well PCR plate onto a thermal cycler block, A1 back left; slide the cover forward, pull the lever down
instruction: Load the capped PCR plate onto the thermal cycler's block with well A1 at the back left, then close the heated cover.
context: PCR is among the most common procedures in molecular biology labs, and in most research labs every run starts with a plate loaded by hand. Thermal cyclers sit in nearly every molecular-biology lab, and current cyclers share this closure: seat the plate, then clamp a heated lid onto it. The GeneAmp 9700 manual: "Place the ... Plate onto the sample block so that the well numbered A1 is located at the upper left corner"; "Slide the heated cover forward ... ensure that the cover is pulled completely forward"; "Pull the lever down to engage the heated cover and the sample tray." The skill: lower 96 conical wells blind into 96 block wells together, keep A1 at the back left, and close the cover in order (slide fully forward, then lever down) only once the plate is down in the block.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table. Thermal cycler: Applied Biosystems GeneAmp PCR System 9700 with its 96-well sample block module, about 26 x 28 x 41 cm (H x W x D), powered off and cold; its front faces the robot, front edge at x 14, centred at y +16 (in front of the left arm, where the arm reaches the block's top). Its heated cover starts slid back with the lever up, so the block is open. Plate: MicroAmp Optical 96-Well Reaction Plate (N8010560), polypropylene, semi-skirted, 0.2 mL wells, 9 mm pitch, 127.8 x 85.5 mm, empty, capped with a MicroAmp 96-Well Full Plate Cover (N8010550). Holder: the plate starts in a MicroAmp Splash-Free 96-Well Support Base (4312063), A1 at the back left, centred at x 20, y +38 (to the robot's left of the cycler, beside its front half). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: 0 at any time if: the plate is dropped (falls more than 1 cm), lands upside down, or is set down anywhere but its support base or the block (its centre over neither); the cover is slid forward or the lever pulled at any time while the plate overlaps the block with any deck corner 5 mm or more above seated; the cover or lever is moved while a gripper holds the plate. Otherwise, from the final 1 s: 0.25: the plate engaged (all four deck corners within 1 mm of seated) but turned 180 degrees; 0.5: engaged with A1 at the back left, the cover not fully forward (more than 1 mm short of its end stop); 0.75: the same, the cover fully forward, the lever not latched down at its stop; 1.0: the same, the lever down to its stop, and both grippers 1 cm or more from plate, cover and lever (0.75 if a gripper is still within 1 cm). Every other end state, including doing nothing, scores 0. Real trial: a levelled close-up camera on a stand against the cycler's right side looks across the block, its lens at seated + 5 mm (so heights read without parallax); that height is marked once as a line on the frame by sighting a plate set on 5 mm spacers on the block; nothing stands on the cycler's left side, where the plate is carried in. On every frame where the cover starts moving forward, no deck corner may show above the line. Afterwards: a rock test (seated: it does not rock when a corner is pressed) and a photo of the cut corner and A1 label for the plate, and a photo of the cover fully forward and the lever down before opening. Drops, set-downs elsewhere, upside-down landings and moves made while holding the plate are judged from the video, hands-off from its final frames.
reset_notes: Lift the lever, slide the cover back, lift the plate out by its edges (rock it gently if it sticks), and put it back on the support base with A1 at the back left. Replace the plate or cover (about $3) if it cracks or the cover lifts. Nothing is used up. Cost: a used 9700 with a 96-well block (about $100-250; a for-parts unit is fine only if its cover slide, lever and 96-well block work; it stays off), a plate, a full plate cover and a support base.
fidelity: Rigid PhysX, 20 Hz. The block is a fixed mesh with 96 conical wells; the plate one rigid body of 96 convex well hulls and its cap mat (no flex). The cover is a sliding carriage with an end stop. The lever turns only once the cover is fully forward; until it latches at its stop a return stiffness stands in for the cam's resistance (est. 20 N at the bar) and the cam lowers a sprung platen onto the plate. The real pull force is measured on the unit before trials. Inner sizes are estimates.
